content: 1. Vemurafenib: Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate (Inhaled): Posaconazole increases the risk of QTc prolongation and toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when combining vilanterol with other QTc-prolonging agents due to potential cardiovascular effects. 3. Vilazodone: Posaconazole increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 4. Vinblastine: Posaconazole increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs due to increased risk of neurotoxicity and other adverse effects. 5. Vincristine: Posaconazole increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs due to increased risk of neurotoxicity, SIADH, and other adverse effects. 6. Vincristine Liposomal: Posaconazole increases vincristine liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs due to increased risk of neurotoxicity, SIADH, and other adverse effects. 7. Vorapaxar: Posaconazole increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Voriconazole: Posaconazole increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Abemaciclib: Posaconazole increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the prior dose. 10. Albuterol: Both albuterol and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Alfuzosin: Both alfuzosin and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Almotriptan: Posaconazole increases almotriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Alprazolam: Posaconazole increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Aluminum Hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Amiodarone: Posaconazole increases amiodarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and amiodarone increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Amitriptyline: Both amitriptyline and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Amlodipine: Posaconazole increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Amoxapine: Both amoxapine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Apalutamide: Posaconazole increases apalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 20. Aprepitant: Posaconazole increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Arformoterol: Both arformoterol and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Aripiprazole: Posaconazole increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both artemether/lumefantrine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Posaconazole also increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Atogepant: Posaconazole increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Atomoxetine: Both atomoxetine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Atorvastatin: Posaconazole increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Posaconazole increases bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Bedaquiline: Both bedaquiline and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 29. Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Posaconazole increases benzhydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 30. Berotralstat: Posaconazole increases berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Betrixaban: Posaconazole increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 32. Bexarotene: Posaconazole increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Bortezomib: Posaconazole increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Brentuximab Vedotin: Posaconazole increases brentuximab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 35. Brexpiprazole: Posaconazole increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 36. Budesonide: Posaconazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Buprenorphine (Subdermal Implant): Posaconazole increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for signs of overmedication. Implant removal may be necessary if dose adjustment is not possible. 38. Buprenorphine (Long-Acting Injection): Posaconazole increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Transition back to a dose-adjustable buprenorphine formulation if toxicity occurs. 39. Buspirone: Posaconazole increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Busulfan: Posaconazole increases busulfan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Calcifediol: Posaconazole affects vitamin D metabolism by inhibiting CYP enzymes, potentially altering calcifediol levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust calcifediol dose as needed. 42. Calcium Carbonate: Calcium carbonate decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cannabidiol: Posaconazole increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose. 44. Capmatinib: Posaconazole increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Carbamazepine: Posaconazole increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while carbamazepine decreases posaconazole levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cariprazine: Posaconazole increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dose reduction is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 47. Ceritinib: Posaconazole increases ceritinib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Chlordiazepoxide: Posaconazole increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Chlorpromazine: Both chlorpromazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Ciclesonide (Inhaled): Posaconazole increases ciclesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
